Climate: Temperate, closest to Coba Plateau (part of the Holy Land island), and also to the Igsh Military District.

Affiliation: Imperial allod, the site of a research base.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I've never had occasion to visit Edge Isle. It got its name because it often appears near the Holy Land. No wonder the League and the Empire strove to capture it, to use it as an additional base. Our side proved quicker. But now access to the island is forbidden. The Xadaganian garrison defending the Edge has betrayed the Empire! Evidently there were demon cultists among them who managed to cloud the soldiers' minds. Or perhaps the whole thing is down to the astral worm that has dug itself in in the middle of the island. They say it can have a destructive effect on the mind. Elizaveta Rysina herself recently summoned me and questioned me about the heroes of the Empire. The thing is, at present our side has no way to send a punitive expedition to the island. And yet the traitors must be punished! And the island cleansed of demons!

Bosses: Cultist Captain, Garm, Astral Worm.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: Based on the Hickut Shard (Enemy Nest).

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Temperate, closest to Coba Plateau (part of the Holy Land island), and also to the Igsh Military District.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, the site of a demon hunters' base.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

It's an ancient fortress, a venerable one. His-to-ri-cal! The Kanians built it even before the Cataclysm, when they were laying the Abatis Line — a long chain of fortifications against orc raids. How many times it was besieged, how many times burnt to the ground — and every time it was rebuilt. So it stood right up until the catastrophe, and then, together with other shards of the old world, it was lost in the Astral. And now, centuries later, the Demon Hunters found it — dilapidated, but all in one piece. Some say it was the courage of many generations of defenders that preserved it, others insist on an astral anomaly... Be that as it may, the Hunters rebuilt it, reinforced it with meteorite shards and turned it into one of their most powerful strongholds. Demons are afraid to sail within cannon shot of it!

Bosses: Blitzkrieg, Zugunder, Paunch, Kaput.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by forest creatures and nature spirits.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

A strange little place... Either that island really exists, or it is a mirage, a phantom, a delusion. That island is covered with dense forests and deep swamps. All sorts of creatures live there, some sentient and some not so much. I saw kikimoras, satyrs, I even saw a talking fox! And most importantly — there are ghosts there without number! Mostly Kanians, seemingly alive and yet not. And they all obey the mistress of that place, Ziva is her name, I think — whether a human, or a bird, or some kind of spirit altogether. A peaceful little place; the mistress was welcoming to us that time, gave us rest and shelter. Only I heard from other travellers that some misfortune happened there recently — whether an unhappy love or some curse... In short, I would think twice about putting in at Iriy without holy water and loaded cannons!

Bosses: Bosk, Mister and Missus, Naiad, Marena.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by forest fauna and spirits.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Isle of Far-Far-Away? Hm... As an acquaintance of mine put it: "Calm, smooth, and the grace of Tensess." And where does such a strange name come from? Well, it's a funny story. Long ago, before the Cataclysm, one remote Kanian province had a name so jaw-breaking that it wasn't preserved even in official charters. And the inhabitants themselves jokingly called their land the Kingdom of Far-Far-Away. It was a real backwater... Forest, forest and nothing but forest! Thousands of hectares of solid green. And it was ruled by a guardian — the living soul of the forest. They say whoever entered that forest with ill thoughts never came out again. Well, after the Cataclysm only a pitiful scrap of that forest remained. But it held out and did not melt away in the astral. And the guardian, they say, survived too. Knowledgeable people told me that her magic still protects the island. Every traveler can count on shelter and rest under the canopy of the age-old trees. But Light forbid you anger the mistress of the forest! If you try to turn the local animals into shashlik, you won't have time to blink before you're turned into cutlets yourself.

Bosses: Forest Spirit, Veleslav Dubov, Blackmarin, Forest Guardian.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, the site of a Kanian hamlet.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Do you know the story of the Isle of the Damned? No? Well, it's not the kind of story you tell children at bedtime... A sad story, a bad one. A story about how the darkness in the soul is more terrible than the Darkness outside. On a distant island lost in the Astral there was a small village. Good people lived there, honest, hard-working. And among them were two young lovers, Ivan and Maria. They loved each other ever so dearly. When the time came they were wed, all proper and fitting, and began to live happily and prosper. That would be the end of the fairy tale... Only you and I don't live in a fairy tale. There was a certain man in that village, an outsider. A bad man, an envious one. He could not look calmly upon the newlyweds' happiness, upon Maria's beauty — and she was a lovely girl, the picture of health. He was terribly jealous of Ivan. Before the young couple were wed he kept making advances to Maria, and each time was sent packing, and a couple of times got a punch in the face from Ivan. And once they were married, he lost his mind altogether from black envy. He decided to destroy the young couple. By deceit he obtained Maria's wedding ring, the love letter Ivan had sent her before the wedding, and the bride's bouquet, which had stood unwithered after the wedding, and with the help of these things he laid a terrible curse on the young couple. From that curse both of them soon went to their graves. And so they were buried together. But the evil did not go unpunished — the curse fell upon the whole island, and the villain himself was not spared. He died and turned into vicious undead, and his cronies and accomplices became skeletons. The restless souls of the young couple remained in the grave, and there is no bright path for them while the curse lies upon them. I beg you — free the innocent souls, lift the curse! To do so you will first need to find the ring, the letter and the flowers the villain used for the curse and bring them to the young couple's grave, and then set their restless souls free. Well, will you take on this good deed?

Bosses: Heartbreaker, Shishimora, Korosten, Ivan Neladov and Maria Neladova.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Contested island.

Addendum: Over time it was reworked into an Astral Dominion island.

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Wasteland, closest to the Cradle.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by the Overlord's servants.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I know about this island only from scraps of information that fell into the hands of Imperial intelligence. In short, it went like this. In one of the sectors an Imperial reconnaissance ship discovered an island not marked on the maps. The captain made several ferrotypes of the island and sent them as an urgent message to the capital. The message said that the captain had decided to carry out reconnaissance. They have not made contact since. You see, this island, which was given the name the Jail, is the prison of the Overlord himself! The ferrotypes show exhausted prisoners locked inside energy domes, and all the passages are blocked by force fields. The territory is patrolled by the Overlord's close servants and battle machines. What's more, there are creatures there that the Committee's experts have identified as high-ranking Wormfaces. According to their theory, it is they who are running what goes on in the Jail at the moment. Which, you'll agree, is somewhat strange — after all, the Wormfaces betrayed the Overlord. From this I can draw one certain conclusion and two guesses. The conclusion: the island is the Overlord's prison, where his servants keep undesirable adventurers. The guesses are these. First, the Wormfaces have somehow managed to subjugate the Overlord's servants. Second, they are hiding from everyone, and we will most likely never see the crew that landed on the shore again. I wouldn't advise you to go there without the support of at least one battleship, or better two. Some mysteries are better never solved...

Bosses: Bloody Executioner, Farakh, the Overlord's Punishment, Provost.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: atlasDescription

Oh, Boyar Jeer is a living legend! Though "living" depends on how you look at it... He is a necromancer, one of the best in the world. Some even say he is a Great one! Whether that's the truth or idle talk, I don't know: for many years now he has lived alone on his estate, talking only with the dead. His peasants are another matter: cheerful, talkative, and not poor either — if the goods are good, they always have a coin to spare. Though a merchant I know was there recently and told me something strange. He steps off the ship, lays out his wares, and the peasants don't so much as glance his way: they all stand stock-still, staring at one point. He looked closer and saw what seemed like a ghostly mist hanging over them all... He took to his heels right away! Whether it's true or not, I don't know — I sell it as I bought it! If you happen to be there — maybe you'll find out the truth?
atlasDescription

Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, a Kanian estate.

Story:

Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Oh, Boyar Jeer is a living legend! Though "living" — that depends on how you look at it... He is a necromancer, one of the best in the world. They even say he is a Great Mage! Whether they tell the truth or lie, I do not know: for many years he has lived alone on his estate, talking only to the dead. His peasants are another matter: merry, talkative, and not poor either — if the goods are good, they always have money. True, a merchant I know was there recently and told a strange thing. He comes off his ship, he says, lays out his goods, and the peasants don't even look his way: they all stand stock-still, staring at one point. He looked closer and saw that a ghostly mist seemed to spread over all of them... He took to his heels from there! Whether it's true or not, I do not know — I sell it as I bought it! If you are there — maybe you will find out the truth?

Story allod:

Catherina sent the heroes to Jeer to learn the skill of speaking with the dead. The problem was that Jeer took no apprentices. So a special approach had to be found. The heroes went to him and left empty-handed — Jeer defeated them and threw them into his dungeon. Only with the help of the Bogatyr whom Catherina had sent with them did they manage to break their chains and leave the prison. And on the way they freed another sorceress — Vasilissa Artful, who also thirsted for forbidden knowledge. The freed Vasilissa had a plan for making Jeer take apprentices after all. For that his death had to be found, and Jeer had hidden his death in a needle. He put the needle in a drake, the drake in a hare, and the hare in a chest, which he hung on a black oak. It was not easy to find Jeer's death, but they did manage to obtain it. And the old man had no choice but to agree to teach the heroes the language of the dead. And the needle in which his death was sealed stayed with Vasilissa.

Bosses: Clockwork Madman, Ill-Rot, Raven Tome, Vasilissa Artful.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Tropical, closest to the Pearl Ring.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Draconids.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I know little about the jungles of Mboa-Mboa. Once we went far, far away, into the very deepest layers of the Astral. We were already thinking of turning back when land appeared on the horizon. We came closer and gasped — what beauty! Everything green, blooming, fragrant, butterflies of every colour of the rainbow flying about, monkeys jumping from palm to palm... Not an island — paradise! Well, that is what we thought until we went ashore. And there... mercy me! I had not seen such hungry creatures in a long time! Huge snakes, bloodsucking mosquitoes, crocodiles with jaws like a trap. So we ran back to the ship, and ran straight into the local aborigines — and next to them the crocodiles seemed a trifle. The scoundrels almost cut us to ribbons. Little, but vicious! After that it only got worse — we escaped the forest folk and ran into Draconids. They gladly invited us to dinner, with us in the role of first course, second course and dessert, so we ran back twice as fast! In short, I will never set foot in those jungles again. To the demons with such cruises!

Bosses: Swiss, Zuul, Boomer, Tom-Tom.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island.

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a former gibberling settlement (captured by demons).

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Frost and cold — that is all I can say about Kyoltmark. I have not been there myself, but I know that one of the first gibberling ships was once wrecked on that icy rock. When League ships did eventually discover the rock a few years later, the surviving gibberlings had already settled on that miserable scrap of land, made themselves at home and flatly refused to leave the island that had become their home. But not so long ago misfortune struck — astral demons attacked the island. And what is strangest of all, they did not slaughter the inhabitants but took them captive. They say a mighty demon called the Thought Catcher turned all the gibberlings into his slaves, and now they serve him faithfully and devotedly. A terrible fate! If you find yourself on that island, you will not avoid a fight with the crazed gibberlings. Strike without pity — only empty shells are left of the locals, and the demons control their will!

Bosses: Fiend, Guur'Maan, Sharpclaw, Thought Catcher.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Desert, closest to the Catacombs.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by lizards.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Surely you're not planning to join the Historians? Any Historian would give his right hand without a second thought to explore Koch-Itzmahl. Just imagine — a fully preserved temple from the heyday of the June empire. Not those pitiful ruins scattered everywhere, but a complete temple complex. I confess I only glimpsed it, and even then I nearly fell overboard in surprise! Bas-reliefs, frescoes, statues, carved columns... Ah, and how many secrets it hides, how many treasures... But there is no way to get to them! Lizards have overrun the whole island. When we tried to put ashore, they pelted us with spears, burned a huge hole in the sail with a fireball, and kept promising to tear out our hearts and lay them on the altar of their ancestors. Their chief, Shisskh, raged most of all. Ooh, vicious creatures! We had to turn round urgently and move on empty-handed. Clearing the temple of the lizards' presence is a good deed and pleasing to the Light... and a profitable one besides!

Bosses: Caiman, Lion, Bloodberry, Shisskh the Seven-Fingered.

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Temperate, closest to Coba Plateau (part of the Holy Land), and also the Igsh Military District.

Affiliation: Imperial allod; a research base is located here.

Story:

We are met by a crowd of vicious undead and the only living man, Iov Milin. He reports to us that this laboratory was engaged in research into necromagic and Tep's technologies. The laboratory was headed by Yaver Gover, a Zem scientist. However, according to Iov, Yaver was not in his right mind and performed strange experiments on the personnel. Iov reported this to General Zubin, but he wouldn't listen. Our task is to reach Mark Grobin, the commissar, and use a secret artifact to inform the Committee of what has happened. After the communication session, the Committee sends reinforcements here (most likely a cleanup squad), and we are ordered to kill Yaver Gover. After the victory we get his diary, from which we learn that he was trying to synthesize Tep's plague, and that he succeeded. He himself survived, since he had already lived through Tep's plague, as did one of the soldiers — Iov Milin. Gover's last entry shows that he intended to capture Milin and study him most thoroughly, in order to understand the cause of his resistance to the Plague.

Bosses: General Plague, Yaver Gover.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Contested island.

Addendum: Over time the island was remade, partly changing the story. It was also reworked into an Isle of the Astral Dominion.

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Temperate, closest to the Frontier.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by aviaks and harpies.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Oh, that is a very interesting place. And a dangerous one! The Land of a Thousand Wings is a jumble of cliffs and the fragments of ancient buildings destroyed centuries ago. Three islands are linked by narrow little bridges that offer a dizzying view. And the Land of a Thousand Wings is inhabited by the only ones who can exist there without the constant risk of falling into the Astral or breaking their necks on the mountain slopes. I am talking about aviaks and harpies. As far as I understood, the aviaks came to the Land of a Thousand Wings first, while the harpies invaded the island much later, and it all ended in a big fight. But somehow Cual the Stormbearer, the aviak elder, managed to tame the unruly harpies. He and the queen of the harpies made peace, and now these two peoples live in complete harmony, helping each other in every way. I even suspect that between Cual himself and Olivia the Temptress there is something more than a business relationship. But that is beside the point. When I was a guest on that island, I was always amazed by Cual's wisdom and lively mind. He even managed to tame a wild manticore that lived in the ruins of an old temple! But in recent years the aviaks have shut themselves off from the rest of the world, accused both the League and the Empire of greed and stupidity, and deal harshly with anyone who dares to set foot on their land. I do not know what caused such sudden hatred of other peoples. Perhaps you will manage to find out the reason? But if you really are going to the Land of a Thousand Wings — get ready for a fierce battle!

Bosses: Olivia the Temptress, Silverwing, Murka, Cual the Stormbearer.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

[Map missing]

Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, a settlement with a fortress.

Story:

The allod was part of Kania (most likely located territorially near Kvatoh). We are met by a Seasoned Sailor; seeing our astral ship, he asks for help and directs us to the Great Mage of this allod. Svetalan, the Great Mage, tells us that the allod was attacked by astral creatures (demons); part of the retinue went off to defend the settlement, but there is still no news of them. And we are asked to find the survivors and help them cope with the scourge. We fought our way to the voivode; he told us that a hundred or so soldiers went to scout at the mill, and while the voivode and the survivors gather their strength, we go scouting. We defeat a Demon Scout and find the scouts hiding in the mill. They say they noticed some people in hoods on the other bank — apparently cultist conspirators. We kill the cultists and their leader. We return to Svetalan to tell him what happened, but the demons have already got into the town. We must fight our way to the chief demon and defeat him. After the victory over the boss, the Great Mage says that as a sign of gratitude we may stay with them on the allod, and also that, if his granddaughter survived, he will introduce her to us.

Bosses: Ferocious Demon Scout, Master Cultist, Demon Boss.

Climate: Temperate, closest to the Astral Graveyard.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, elementals, undead.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I had a friend — Roman Kuzin. A traveler, an explorer. And ill luck carried him to the Lost Isle. There has been no word from him since... The Lost Isle is a legend. The legend of a Pyramid of Tep that acquired a mind of its own and stamps out undead, putting Sparks into dead bodies. It is known that whoever manages to defeat the Pyramid will get a treasure. That is exactly what Romka dreamed of. He gathered information about the island. I will share it with you if you undertake to find this island and save my comrade. On the Lost Isle you will meet magical elementals that are the embodiment of the Pyramid's power. You will meet many undead created by it. By destroying them you will be able to reach the Pyramid itself, where you must find a way to switch it off. And if you do that and the Pyramid stops working, its treasure will be your reward. Well? Will you take on the job?

Bosses:

ver. 1: Pulsating Magic Elemental, Cobweb Spider, Pyramid Guardian.

ver. 2: Pulsating Magic Elemental, Cobweb Spider, Zinoviy Semetry, Crusher.

t: atlasDescription

For as long as I've been ploughing the Astral, this islet was always just a frozen lump of rock — no life, no vegetation. And recently it changed as if by magic: now streams flow there, trees blossom, and there are even some little houses! I put in to shore, and more wonders — creatures live there such as I've never seen in my life. Like Gibberlings, but not Gibberlings, fluffy and long-eared. They are friendly and hospitable, only somehow skittish. They say another tribe lives beyond the mountains, and they are afraid their kin might go to war against them. I wished them the help of the Light, and they gave me a strange look and sent me on my way. A riddle, not an island, honestly!
atlasDescription

Climate: Taiga, closest to Siveria.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited mainly by Tekyans.

Story:

Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

For as long as I've been ploughing the Astral, that little island was always just a frozen lump of rock — no life, no vegetation. And then recently it was transformed as if by magic: now streams run there, trees bloom, there are even some little houses standing! I put in to shore, and more wonders: creatures live there such as I've never seen in my life. Something like gibberlings, but not gibberlings — fluffy and big-eared. They are friendly and hospitable, only somehow skittish. They say another tribe lives beyond the mountains, and they fear their kin may come to make war on them. I wished them the help of the Light, but they gave me a strange look and sent me on my way. That island is a riddle, upon my word!

Story allod:

Catherina sent the heroes to discover the source of a great power near Umoir, and gave them a Knight to help — the warrior Claire Brightley. Arriving on Lumix Isle (as the island where that sorcery was being worked was called), they witnessed yet another miracle: instead of bare rock and ice, a settlement had appeared on the allod. And not just any settlement, but a village of the Tekyans, who had all perished — destroyed by Tep — and until then had existed only in the Illusory World. Yet these Tekyans were real creatures of flesh and blood. They remembered everything that had happened to them in Tequatl on Irdrich, but how they had come to be on Lumix Isle they did not really understand themselves. They wished to summon their patron Genlun, and to that end had built a statue of him. And Genlun did indeed answer the call, which, however, roused the wrath of Claire, who, being a Paladin, did not wish to have any dealings with a pagan god. Genlun related that a few days earlier something like a shining palm had taken them from Tequatl together with their houses and moved them here, while at the same time trying to erase all memory of their crocodile patron. Genlun sensed that there was another Tekyan village on the island whose people had already stopped believing in him, and he suggested going there. When the heroes and Claire reached the second village, it turned out that the Tekyans living there now worshipped the Light. But their faith was far from kind: to prove that the heroes were not pagans, these Tekyans proposed that they die and be resurrected. Not even Brightley agreed to that, so they had to pacify the fluffy zealots. Further on, the path through the village led them to June ruins, where the captive Klavdia awaited them. She revealed that it was her handiwork — both Lumix Isle and the Tekyans, whom she had managed to bring into the real world with the power of Tep's Spark. And the one who had taken her captive was none other than the Servant of Light himself, the fire-haired angel from Purgatory. Now the heroes and Claire had to fight him as well. What lay behind his displeasure, no one could yet say. But Claire decided to stay on Lumix Isle to keep an eye on Genlun and on the Light-worshipping Tekyans.

Bosses: Li-Ter, Plamennik, Fluffy, Claire Brightley.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Desert, closest to Kirah.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by cultists.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

You probably know what happened on Irdrich. Tep, an ancient necromancer of the Zem people, fancied himself a god and prepared a whole army of mechanoids to enslave all of Sarnaut. In the face of such danger our troops joined forces with the Leaguers and crushed the viper after all. But though Tep is dead, his cause lives on. Every now and then heroes stumble upon lairs of cultists who don't know about the death of their god or refuse to believe in it. And sometimes it's the other way round: some of Tep's slaves turned away from their master. One soldier told me that while the cultists and mechanoids were hacking away at the united army, a rusty barge quietly pulled away from the shore and sailed off in an unknown direction. Maybe it's just a tall tale: I sell it for what I bought it. But if you come across an island of rusty renegades somewhere in the depths of the astral, don't be surprised.

Bosses: Fill-o-Matic, Nomarkh Megavolt, Negus Augment, Integral.

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Taiga, closest to Siveria.

Affiliation: Imperial allod, an industrial town of the Empire.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Metalville... A vivid example of what can happen to soldiers when they have a lot of free time not taken up by drill or reading regulations. Some ten years ago Metalville was a small mining town; then, when the mine ran dry, it was sealed and the town was handed over to the Imperial Army as a training ground. "Blues" against "Reds", just like in Igsh. And everything went strictly according to plan, until the general of the "Blues", a hulking orc named Gire the Merciless, quarrelled in front of all his officers with the general of the "Reds", Steel the Highlander. They swore at each other up and down, and parted ways. The "Red" had already forgotten the quarrel, but the "Blue" took such offence that he raised his regiment on alarm in the middle of the night and led it to the attack. He had decided to wash away the insult in blood! Under cover of darkness they hacked most of the "Reds" into mincemeat, and when dawn broke they realized that all they had to look forward to now was a tribunal and a firing squad by a brick wall. And with truly orcish stubbornness they decided to go all the way. Gire declared himself a great chieftain, the orcs the master race, and everyone else dust under soldiers' boots, and set about building his great Empire. But there was a snag: the astral ships had managed to leave Metalville. So now the newly minted chieftains of the Empire are stuck in the besieged town, fighting the remnants of the "Reds" and dreaming of a new orcish empire under the leadership of the great and wise chieftain Gire — curse him, the treacherous brute!

Bosses: Negus Mengulis, Rowdy Raja, Bubbah Two Fingers, Gire the Merciless.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a colony of the Aoidoi.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Ah, the Aoidoi. They've only just come into the world, and they've already built themselves cities — for all to see. New Bay is only just being built, but it will be a beautiful city! You can't deny these stoneheads their courage, of course — the sector where the Bay stands is literally teeming with crazed monsters. Let's hope no disaster comes of it... I've heard, by the way, that some demons don't want to feud with them, but offer friendship instead. Hogwash, if you ask me. If the Aoidoi trust those creatures, they're as naive as children. Better be careful — demons are no joke.

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Temperate, closest to Coba Plateau.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by pirates.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

At the dawn of astral navigation, when there were no visors yet and the first ships groped their way through the astral almost by touch, lighthouses were built on the islands that were discovered. A lighthouse's light could be seen from very far away, and it signaled: "Sail here, it's safe." Many sailors lost in the astral thanked fate more than once for a lighthouse glimpsed in the distance. Later, as astral navigation developed, lighthouses became less important. With a modern visor, astrolabe and navigator, getting lost in the astral is practically impossible. So nowadays lighthouses are for the most part a tribute to tradition and a place where you can rest in peace, spend the night and hear the latest news. But recently I received unpleasant news: a gang of astral pirates has seized one of the old lighthouses and is using it as a trap. As soon as a ship heading for the lighthouse's light moors at the pier, it is boarded at once, plundered and smashed to splinters, and the whole crew is sent to walk the plank into the astral! Beasts! Barbarians! So many innocent people have suffered because of them. They must be stopped at any cost! And the treasures, if you find them, keep for yourself — the dead have no use for them anymore...

Bosses: Zavid Ushkuynikov, Yasskul "Jolly" Roger, Sturdy Door, Feint the Greedy.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by … .

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Old Loam? And why are you interested? Look me in the eye! Don't dodge!

Hm... I suppose one can discuss state secrets with you. Of course I know about that island. There's nothing particularly remarkable about it — a village of poor peasants, a pine forest, a cold climate. That's probably exactly why the Committee chose it as a testing ground for its experiments. Observing Kanians in their everyday environment! Reconnaissance operations! Espionage! Ah, it reminds me of my old days... All I've heard from the sailors is that strange things began happening to the animals in the forest near Old Loam, and some of the villagers vanished without a trace. My advice is to give the island a wide berth and keep out of the Committee's affairs. Otherwise, heaven forbid, they'll have to kill you. That would be awkward. You don't have any doubt that their actions are aimed solely at the good of the Empire, do you?

Bosses: Hut, Snezhana Zaykina, Bewitched Peasant, Veres.

[Map missing]

Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, a colony.

Story:

We are met by Ivan Poklyovych (the village headman). He tells us that they had been living peacefully on this colony for 3 years, but then pirates of the "Insidious" clan sailed to the allod, after them a ship of the House de Lua, and now, he says, us. He asks us to help deal with the pirates and sends us to Vitold de Lua. Vitold informs us that the pirates attacked because of the battery that powered the sphere of astral resistance, an ancient artifact that protects space the way the great mages do. The Sphere is not working because the battery is missing, and for now "I am holding the island; the inhabitants were very lucky that I happened to be here in time. The pirates' ship has been destroyed and they cannot leave the allod, but they don't want to hand over the stolen battery. It is with one of the officers — there are only 4 of them, so we won't have to search long." On the way to the pirates, Ivan asks us to rescue the captured villagers. We defeat the officers, but Uryg the Insidious begs for mercy and says that the Elf is no great mage, but a cultist who hired them to steal the battery; when he sailed in after them, the first thing he did was destroy their ship. He demands the battery and says he will save us from this island if we give it to him. He advises us to give it to the girl from the church — she should know — but she is somewhat shady. We take the battery and return it to the church, giving it to Taisia. She puts it back in place, and her reason returns to her. After that we go to rescue the captured villagers, and then to kill the impostor. After the victory over Vitold, the headman thanks us.

Bosses: Urgan Big Axe, Uryuk Long Arm, Nakhrap the Wrathful, Uryg the Insidious, Vitold de Lua.

[Map missing]

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: League allod, a colony of Kanians and a settlement of Forestfolk.

Story:

We are met by the Kanian Leader. According to him, their ship was wrecked during an astral storm, and they ended up on this island. At first they wanted to make repairs quickly, but in the end they grew used to this quiet, peaceful allod and are now settling in here. He asks us to help the settlers, since there aren't enough hands and there is a lot of work. We meet the Cook; she asks us to take food to the fishermen. And another Kanian woman asks for her help: she cooks and tends the cauldrons, and the men, the fishermen, haven't brought the fish yet. We need to help them deliver it, because it's already time to cook. After we bring the fishermen food, they thank us and ask us to help explore the wondrous valley and the lake while they organize the fishery. We stroll through the valley all the way to the lake. Then we dive into it and discover that in the depths there is some kind of tunnel with a magical barrier. We return and tell the fishermen about it. They say that they don't understand such things — talk to our Leader. We return to the settlement and bring the women fish. They invite us to come and eat when we have time. The Leader says about the tunnel that we may explore it, but carefully, so as not to bring trouble upon the settlement. They want to stay and live here. After passing through the tunnel, we surface on the other side of the island and find a settlement of natives there. We are met by a Shaman, who says he doesn't mind neighbors, but he cannot decide such matters alone. We must find the elder; he is hunting by the big lake. By the Lake, in the thickets, we find the Chief. He says that if we help kill the Unthinkable Monster, then they (the Forestfolk) agree to live in alliance with the humans. We dive in and defeat the Hydra. After that the Chief says that he has a daughter, and the Kanians have men; to seal the alliance forever, the two clans must be joined in marriage. We return to the settlement and tell them everything that happened. The Leader thanks us for the help and says that the Forestfolk will have their bridegroom. An alliance is important, since we have decided to stay here.

Bosses: Unthinkable Monster Hydra.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Yes, I have seen that islet. It really is a graveyard, and it really is peaceful. An old Kanian cemetery, one more forgotten shard of a perished world. A quiet place, a sad one. Dark trees, mist over the marshes, leaning gravestones... And in the depths some shadows drift and little lights flicker. Grief and dread simply breathe from it. I flew past it once, but decided not to land. Trust my experience: don't disturb the dead, or they will disturb you so badly you'll remember it all your life!

Climate: Temperate, closest to the Lower City.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, the site of a pirate base (fort).

Story:

Astral island:

Eugene Silberpod (Astral Adventurer):

Jolly Roger Bay! They say that a thousand years ago there really was a sea here, and a bay — and even then the Brethren of the Coast feasted here! Over his long life Feint plundered a great deal, and not just gold. Rare books, magical artifacts, ancient relics — anything your heart desires! Only he buried them in the most godforsaken spot. The living don't walk there, but the dead positively dance about. Do you know who they are? Feint's crew. He wasn't a mage, but he remembered the astral superstitions. They say that if you shove a black spot between a dead sailor's teeth, he'll never know rest, and will wander on until he gets rid of it.

Story island:

The pursuit of Klavdia led the heroes to Takalik Harbor, home of Eugene Silberpod, a slippery rogue if ever there was one. He agreed to escort them to the Bay. Jolly Roger Bay! They say that a thousand years ago there really was a sea here, and a bay — and even then the Brethren of the Coast feasted here! Over his long life Feint plundered a great deal, and not just gold. Rare books, magical artifacts, ancient relics — anything your heart desires! Only he buried them in the most godforsaken spot. The living don't walk there, but the dead positively dance about. Do you know who they are? Feint's crew. He wasn't a mage, but he remembered the astral superstitions. They say that if you shove a black spot between a dead sailor's teeth, he'll never know rest, and will wander on until he gets rid of it. Naturally, Silberpod wished first and foremost to get to the treasure. And this was not his first journey to the Bay; more than once he had tried to get the gold, but it never came into his hands. For the Plague, spreading from the portal to Umoir, had already begun to take hold of the Bay. Silberpod and his companions managed to capture the pirates' fort, and then they had to get through the traps and secrets Feint had left behind. But when they reached the spot where the treasure had been buried, it turned out that someone else had already moved it. The pirate was consumed by insatiable greed, and he ordered the whole island searched, including the cursed ruins. And there he came face to face with one of his old companions — Benny Cakeson. The power of the Plague had turned him into an unknown monster — and now the same fate awaited Eugene Silberpod himself, doomed to become the new guardian of Feint's treasure. The heroes set off through the Ancient Portal to Umoir... And the Bay met its own fate.

Bosses: Badyai, Merry, Shroud Weaver, Kraken.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Temperate, closest to Dane.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by traders and Kanians.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Ah, Plague City is a bad business. Of course, it wasn't always called that — once it was a perfectly ordinary, flourishing city, moderately rich, decently arranged; its rulers even had heads on their shoulders. Not every backwater can manage that, you know — develop some kind of trade, give children an education and keep a firm faith in the Light. In short, it was an outstanding city. And every outstanding thing will have its envious ones. Sometimes, alas, very powerful ones. For some reason a certain warlock came to hate this city — and he had power enough to release the Pestilence, a merciless magical disease that turned the city into an abode of nightmares within a matter of hours. Some tried to fight — to burn the contagion with fire. Others "adapted" and began quickly hauling off everything of value. And the third... They were less lucky — the disease took them, turning them into mindless undead. In the end the cursed city broke away from the allod and was lost in the astral. You can see it here and there — the curse of the Pestilence forces it to relive that terrible day over and over. With all my heart I wish you never to become its witness.

Bosses: Hur the Boiling, Long Arm, Yaver Brand, Devastator.

Type: Medium allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by the Waterfolk Tribe.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

During one of the expeditions an island was discovered that had evidently broken away from the Holy Land. There is a place of power on the island, can you imagine! And the magic of the Light, over which the League and the Empire are fighting, is present there in full measure. The only trouble is that for the locals this miracle has become the basis of a bloody cult. They believe that the source of the Gift of Resurrection is the Scorpion King — a giant beast they call Serket. The Waterfolk and the Forestfolk wage war on each other and offer sacrifices to this scorpion. As you can understand, there can be no question of those poor wretches ever being resurrected. But, in the opinion of the island's inhabitants, this is how they guarantee resurrection for everyone else. This orgy must be stopped. However, the Waterfolk and the Forestfolk will not let you simply challenge their venomous king. You will have to fight them. The Waterfolk are stronger and more dangerous, so the main blow will fall on them. But your chief target is Serket, the Scorpion King.

Bosses: Waterfolk Priest, Gavial, Serket.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Contested island.

Addendum: Based on the World Barque. Over time it was reworked into an Astral Dominion island.

Climate: Tropical, closest to the Pearl Ring and the Tropical Atoll.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by humanoid toads.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Hm-m... I have heard of such an islet in the depths of the Astral, yes, though I confess I have never set foot on it myself. Nasty tales are told about that place. Ships go missing there, or so they say... A pilot I know told me that near that island all the equipment starts playing up, the reactor boils over, and the visor goes completely mad! But that is not all. Once, in some port, I met a thoroughly drunk orc who, by his own account, had served as cook on an Imperial trading schooner. And he told me that their ship had been wrecked on that atoll. He spoke of wandering undead, of some savages who feed on people, of an ugly idol... To be honest, I did not pay much attention to his drunken babble. But you, well, if you decide to put in at that atoll, don't let go of your weapon!

Bosses: Hump, Scabies, Pimple, Dead Captain.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Howlem.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, an ancient abode of the Pridens.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Ravine of Shadows? I've heard of it, I've heard. I haven't been there myself, I won't lie. But a Priden traveler told me that long, long ago — so long that even their Voices barely remember when it was — a huge piece broke off from Howlem, and on it stood some temple. The Pridens believe they angered the First Ones, and the First Ones punished them. I don't know about the curse of the First Ones, but I've heard from astral pirates about a huge mountain in the astral with old ruins rising on its summit. Gentlemen of fortune tried to pick up something valuable there, and barely got away. In a whisper they told how their own shadows came to life and began killing right and left. And when the whole pirate rabble scattered in all directions, ghosts — whether of men or beasts, who knows — stood in their path with weapons in their hands, and not a single one reached the ruins alive. Those who managed to rush back to the ship raced away from that island under full sail. So I reckon that if it was a curse, it still haunts anyone who dares to enter this Ravine...

Bosses: Forgotten, Maas-Risa the Bedazzling, Saad-Brok the Stormbringer, Shoom-Kagat the Black-Handed.

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by the undead.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. I think you know no worse than I do about the ill fame of this place. The patrimony of the noblest aristocrats turned into a den of unclean spirits and the undead. Or rather, so it was until a squad of League daredevils made their way into the very depths of that burrow and put an end to the curse. But what if everything had gone wrong? The mysterious astral is an enigmatic place. Sometimes it lets you see what would have become of familiar places if history had developed differently. The Imperials have nothing to do in Castle Blight — they have troubles enough of their own. But what if Kvatoh had fallen under the rule of the Empire? What if Elizaveta Rysina had sent an elite corps of exorcists to the castle, and the evil entrenched in the castle had taken possession of their souls? If you find yourself in the reflection of Castle Blight, beware: those you meet there are not real priests, not Imperials, and not even people. But the wounds they can inflict on you are quite real... As are the treasures you'll find in the storerooms!

Bosses: Firebliz the Righteous, Svetlana Pravdina, Crucifier, Kirill Pravdin, the Guise-Stealer.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Astral reflection.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Tenebra.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by vampires.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. You know what happened in the Darkblood Citadel. The ancestral nest of the House de Doucer, where all high society once flocked to balls and soirées, turned into a nest of ghouls. Armando de Doucer got in league with Tep and staged a vampire invasion of Kvatoh and Avilon. Only the intervention of heroes like you thwarted his plans... But what if everything had gone differently? Do you know who the worst enemies of vampires are? Werewolves! It seems to have something to do with the blood curse that lies on both of them. If the spires of a galleon palace appear in the mysterious astral, get ready to see what would have happened if the werewolves had got to the ghouls before the heroes of the League. Only don't let your guard down: werewolves hate the likes of you only a little less than bloodsuckers. Mind you don't end up between the hammer and the anvil!

Bosses: Ushan, Rottenfang, Webweaver, Shadow, Zinovy Gorsky.

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Temperate, closest to Gipat.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Wormfaces.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. An ancient temple of a vanished people... To whom did they offer prayers in it? To the One Creator? To local spirits? To great heroes and rulers? What did they sacrifice — incense or someone's hearts? Today no one knows. The temple ruins on Gipat became the stage for the last act of the Play, where the heroes of Sarnaut received the Revelation. I was there too... Now that's a place I'd rather not go back to! But one traveler told me that in the depths of the mysterious astral he saw a reflection of the June Temple: ruins where imps and demon worshippers wander. True, in that temple the cultists dug up some June magitech and are now at war with it, not knowing how to bury it again. He also let slip that at the very end the temple gave him an unpleasant surprise. If you ask me — what could be more unpleasant than what we actually found in it? But you, if you find this reflection, keep your ears open!

Bosses: Fleshwither, Inevitable Death, Ravager, Vur'tazz the Ravager, Soul Sucker.

Climate: Desert, closest to Kirah.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by the undead.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. The name of Tep no longer strikes terror into peaceful folk. This ancient Hickutian sorcerer, who longed to become a god, was destroyed by the heroes of the Empire on the shards of the allod of Irdrich, with some minor help from the brave souls of the League. But what if Tep had not been resurrected? What would have become of his lair if it had never seen its master return? They say that in the depths of the astral one can find a reflection of Irdrich where there is neither a pyramid nor cultists — only the grim inventions of the ancient necromancer, which go on wrecking ships and snuffing out Sparks even without their creator. If you come across this place, be careful: though it is only what might have happened, Tep's reflected machines are no less dangerous than the real ones!

Climate: Temperate, closest to Igsh.

Affiliation: Imperial allod; a laboratory is located here.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. Secret laboratories... The Committee can stamp as many secrecy classifications as it likes, but murder will out: even the lowliest goblin under a fence already knows that our research program has serious problems. Something explodes in one laboratory, something leaks in another, and in a third the head of the lab turns out to be a cultist. And the harder they try to classify it all, the more rumors go around. And rumors have a power of their own. Because the astral... The astral knows how to listen. And now in its depths you can find a reflection that embodies all the scary tales about Imperial laboratories. Mad scientists, cultist spies, inhuman experiments, nightmarish machines and mutilated test subjects — everything idle chatterboxes might spin for you. So if you see a science town behind iron gates somewhere in the astral and decide to go ashore... I hope you have strong nerves!

Bosses: Armando de Doucer, Poisonous Trap, Darksoul Leader, Purger Fire Thrower, Meat Golem.

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Temperate, closest to Igsh.

Affiliation: League allod; a prison is located here.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. Don't you really know about this place? Although... you probably have no need to. Oreshek Fortress is the largest and most impregnable prison in the whole League. They hold the most dangerous cutthroats and butchers there, thieves and swindlers, traitors and rebels. No one has ever escaped from there — where would you run to from an astral island! They say the Committee tried to carry out a special operation there: to free some dangerous rebel and drop him back onto Kvatoh — let Aidenus have a headache. The guards turned out to be no slouches, and our people barely got away... But that's in reality! And somewhere in the depths of the astral a reflection has appeared in which the prisoner got free. And, you know, those who have seen that reflection say it's a good thing the Committee didn't succeed in reality. Unpatriotic, of course, but the last thing we needed was one of the League's mightiest fortresses turned into a bandit nest!

Bosses: Trap, Asyka, Marcel de Doucer, Daring Family, Miroslav Kramolsky.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Astral reflection.

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by cultists.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever come across astral reflections? A most curious phenomenon: an almost exact outward reflection of a place that really exists, in which, however, events unfold quite differently than in the normal world. Is it for me to tell you about Tensess Temple! After all, it was you who had to fight your way through hordes of enemies to uncover the secret of the gift of Light. I'd like to know what you heroes saw there and what the Spark of Tensess told you. But a state secret is a state secret. I'd better tell you what I know about its astral reflection.

A half-ruined sanctuary in the depths of the jungle — the tomb of an ancient mage, a rival of Nezeb himself. You won't find the Spark of Tensess in the reflection, but there will be enemies in abundance. In this the reflection is very close to reality... You'll have to overcome the most dangerous enemies and a whole horde of demons at the very top of the temple. But the reward will be worthy! Who knows, perhaps the reflection will share new secrets with you?

Bosses: Fleshwither, Inevitable Death, Ravager, Vur'tazz the Ravager, Soul Sucker.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Astral reflection.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Temperate, closest to Avilon.

Affiliation: Elven allod, a settlement of the House de Doucer.

Story:

We are met by Patrick de Doucer. He tells us that all those who did not follow Armando have gathered on this allod. The other elven houses would not accept them, and they want nothing to do with the vampires. Patrick asks us to help win back the southern part of the allod from the creatures living there. First, to defeat the granite trolls and their leader, Cliff. Martin de Doucer also has a request for us, but this time to help on the eastern part of the allod. Mantises live there, and it is them we must deal with. The Great Mage Karl de Doucer turns to us. He tells us that for the time being he is protecting the allod from the astral and holding up the shields; he is worried by the presence of lizards on the allod — they are far more dangerous than any trolls or mantises. The lizards are ruled by a creature resembling a draconid, named Oskal. The trouble is that he can't be negotiated with, as with the lizards, and our goal is to make our way into their settlement and destroy Oskal. After clearing the allod of the mantises and trolls, we go to the lizards' altar. There we defeat Oskal. The sentries Patrick and Martin thank us and say that now developing the settlement will be easier. And the Great Mage thanks us and says that he now feels better, since the evil that was hindering him has been defeated.

Bosses: Troll Chief Cliff, Lizard Leader Oskal.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, although representatives of the House de Desirae have settled here.

Story:

After landing on the allod, we are met by the master seeker Scius de Desirae.

According to him, their House was building a galleon ship, but decided to secretly build another ship for personal purposes; however, it rebelled and vanished. They searched for it carefully while concealing what they were doing, and in the end found it wrecked on this allod. We are asked to try to tame it (the galleon). By killing the elementals, we show the galleon our strength. We return to Scius; he thanks us for the help and gives us the ring of the 8 houses, which was supposed to continue the story, but there is no information about it.

Bosses: Great Fire Elemental, Great Water Elemental, Great Ice Elemental, Great Air Elemental.

t: atlasDescription

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by lamias and drakes.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Ugh, what a question! Rotswamp is the vilest place in the Astral. It squelches underfoot, drips down your collar, insects swarm in the mud, and the fog is so thick you can't see your own feet. In short, Rotswamp is the vilest swamp in the world! And how many travellers have vanished there... Wherever you go, you run straight into dangerous creatures! When I had the bad luck to end up in that stinking swamp with an expedition, on the very first day we lost three guards in fights with hydras. Horrible creatures that spit venom, and the oldest hydra, which we nicknamed Echidna, bit a pack horse in half in one go!

At night we were woken by terrible screams — lamias armed to the teeth attacked the camp, cut down the sentry and rushed at us, shouting something about two sisters thirsting for our blood. We barely fought them off! But in retreating we went into the very depths of the swamp, and that is where the main danger lay in wait for us. We had not even had time to wonder why the lamias had stopped pursuing us when a huge drake swooped from the night sky straight onto our party, pouring fire over everything around, while smaller drakes circled overhead, making sure none of us escaped. I survived only by a miracle — I fell into the mud, buried myself in it, and the drakes did not notice me. My comrades were not so lucky… By morning, having waited until the drakes finished their bloody feast and flew away, I crept back to the ship. Utterly exhausted, wounded and covered in mud from head to toe, at the sight of the ship waiting for us I almost wept with relief, and I swore that I would never again set foot in that cursed place!

Bosses: Echidna, Euriala and Stheno, Old Swamper, Venomwing.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: atlasDescription

Don't even ask. You're not supposed to know about this island, and neither am I. It's secret, se-cret, what's not to understand? Oh, all right, I'll whisper what I know. Some experiments were carried out there with the technologies captured in the Dead City. Where they wanted to open the gates, I don't know, and where they did open them, I don't want to know. Why? Because the other day the staff were urgently evacuated from there, and the whole region was marked on the maps as quarantined and strictly off-limits. Want to poke your nose into military secrets? Well, you do love a risk — maybe you'll find something out... No, don't tell me, I don't want to know! Although... well, maybe just in a low voice, in my ear.
atlasSubPlace

Ney is not a very large allod, although it was here that Zayan, together with Skrakan, first succeeded in creating the holding ritual. It lies in the middle of a plain that was once far up in the mountains. The local landmark deserves a mention too — Rakhl-Ney, a tower that is almost the only building on the allod. The Council of Historians now sits in it. The tower itself is a grandiose library, with shelves the size of several houses. Of course, not only books are kept in Rakhl-Ney; there are plenty of artefacts of all kinds here as well. Besides the tower, the sights include an old system of portals leading to a great many allods. This was something like a crossroads where many magical paths of the June tribe converged… It is only a pity that many of the portals no longer work.

Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Imperial allod, a secret base.

Story:

Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Don't even ask. You're not supposed to know about this island, and neither am I. It's secret, se-cret, what's so hard to understand? Oh, all right, I'll whisper what I know. Some experiments were carried out there with technologies captured in the Dead City. Where they meant to open the gates — I don't know, and where they did open them — I don't want to know. Why? Because the other day the personnel were urgently evacuated from there, and the whole region was marked on the maps as quarantined and strictly off-limits. You want to poke your nose into military secrets? Well, you love a risk — maybe you'll find something out... No, don't tell me, I don't want to know! Although... Well, unless it's in a low voice, in my ear.

Story allod:

In the Plagot Ruins, records were found of a temporal anomaly that Skrakan himself had studied. Finding the coordinates of the place was no problem, and the petty crook and thief Urri Miloslavin reported that at the indicated spot stood a Xadaganian base, which Catherina had allowed to be built in exchange for certain Imperial technologies. Intrigued by this base, the heroes set off there. And it turned out that Gates-II was the testing site of a Time Machine built by the Xadaganian genius Alex Everykin. And Alex was ready to travel far into the past — for instance, to see the world before the Cataclysm. But when a temporal portal was opened into Zayan's tower, the heroes and Miloslavin found themselves in the past, while the Zayan of the past ended up in the future, after which the portal closed. What had happened threatened temporal paradoxes, but the heroes managed to find a way back. To return back to the future, they had to use the Grain of Protopower... Alas, on returning and giving the Grain to Zayan, the heroes learned that it was precisely the Grain that Zayan had needed to stabilize the spell known as the Great Experiment. And its loss had caused the Cataclysm to happen. Still, a question remained — was what happened inevitable? And Gates-II did not escape the sad fate that awaited all the Imperial laboratories. No one will ever tell now exactly where the Imperial scholars decided to open a portal... But it is known that the island fell victim to a terrible plague. Was it Tep's plague? Or something even more terrible?

Bosses: Ague, Consumption, Rotgulp, Pandemician.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

Climate: Varied (tropical and wasteland): an oasis inside, the rest of the allod is rock.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by demons.

Story:

We arrive on the allod and, fighting our way through the demons into the dome, meet a Gibberling named Yodo (the master). The Master is indignant that we disturbed him, but decides to teach us great wisdom all the same. The first task he gives is to find the most beautiful, most special water lily. After a long search we return to the Master without having found it. He shares the wisdom that we would never have found it, for all lilies are special and beautiful — one need only notice their beauty. Then, to humble our pride, we must walk around every root of the Great Tree, and without hurrying. When we return to the Master, he wants to test us on Demons and orders us to kill three of each of the 3 kinds that live on the allod beyond the dome, but no more. After the victory over these demons, Yodo gives us a serious trial: to defeat two Demon Leaders, but no more. We defeat them. Yodo says that we are strong, but will we keep our balance on the edge between strength and wisdom? He gives us a last lesson: to kill the Great Demon — he is cunning, and we need to know how to deal with such creatures if they go on the attack against other allods. We overcome this demon too, and in parting Yodo says that we did well and learned wisdom — a pity it wasn't the wisdom he wanted to teach us.

Bosses: Demon Leader Scout, Demon Leader Warrior, Great Demon.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.
